# incident_incident_form (Data Source)

Configure the forms used to declare, accept, update, and resolve incidents.

Each form carries its elements and the expressions those elements can reference.
Escalate forms are not part of this API.

Use this data source to read an existing incident form by ID, including its elements and expressions, without managing it as an `incident_incident_form` resource. The ID of a form is in the dashboard's URL when editing it. Escalate forms are not available through this data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read an existing incident form by its ID, which is in the dashboard's URL when
# editing the form.
data "incident_incident_form" "default_declare" {
  id = "01FCNDV6P870EA6S7TK1DSYDG0"
}

# The full definition is available, so you can (for example) check which custom
# fields a form built in the dashboard asks for.
output "default_declare_custom_fields" {
  value = [
    for element in data.incident_incident_form.default_declare.lifecycle_elements :
    element.custom_field_id if element.element_type == "custom_field"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this incident form

### Read-Only

- `expressions` (Attributes Set) Expressions that make variables available in the scope (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--expressions))
- `form_type` (String) Which form this is. Escalate forms are not part of this API. Possible values are: `declare`, `accept`, `update`, `resolve`, `retrospective`, `custom-fields`.
- `incident_type_id` (String) The incident type this form belongs to. Unset for the organisation's default form of this type.
- `lifecycle_elements` (Attributes List) Elements on this form, in display order. List position is the order: there is no separate rank. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lifecycle_elements))
- `unlock_in_dashboard` (Boolean) Not populated: whether Terraform claims a resource is configuration, and no read endpoint reports it.

<a id="nestedatt--lifecycle_elements"></a>
### Nested Schema for `lifecycle_elements`

Read-Only:

- `can_select_no_value` (Boolean) Whether the user can explicitly choose no value. Only meaningful for custom field elements.
- `config` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lifecycle_elements--config))
- `custom_field_id` (String) The custom field this element edits. Set only when element_type is custom_field.
- `default_value` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lifecycle_elements--default_value))
- `description` (String) Description shown beside this element, as markdown
- `element_type` (String) What this element captures. Possible values are: `name`, `status`, `severity`, `incident_role`, `incident_type`, `summary`, `custom_field`, `timestamp`, `update_message`, `next_update_in`, `triage`, `visibility`, `divider`, `text`, `incident_attachments`, `slack_channel`, `announce_retro_incident`, `enter_post_incident_flow`, `investigation_feedback`.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this element. divider and text elements are matched on this, because they have no natural key.
- `incident_role_id` (String) The incident role this element assigns. Set only when element_type is incident_role.
- `incident_timestamp_id` (String) The incident timestamp this element sets. Set only when element_type is timestamp.
- `placeholder` (String) Placeholder text shown in the empty field
- `required_if` (String) When this element must be filled in. Possible values are: `check_engine_config`, `always_require`, `never_require`.
- `required_if_condition_groups` (Attributes List) The condition groups to apply in this filter. Only one group needs to be satisfied for the filter to pass. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lifecycle_elements--required_if_condition_groups))
- `show_if_condition_groups` (Attributes List) The condition groups to apply in this filter. Only one group needs to be satisfied for the filter to pass. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lifecycle_elements--show_if_condition_groups))
